title: Python attribute-write #4 (type(x).m and type(self).m re-dispatch) and (a81) N8 diamond super — split out of GCLI-156 (DEC-303 a88/a84)
description: Split out of GCLI-156 before building under DEC-303 (a88) (split before building if needed, no ruling needed) because neither shape fits GCLI-156 two-round budget with shape #6. TWO ITEMS. (1) #4 from (a84) item 1: the type(x).m and type(self).m re-dispatch, which MOVED to GCLI-156 out of opum-ai/glyph-cli#236 and per (a84) item 1 gets its own two review rounds. tree-sitter mis-parses type(self).m = v as a PEP 695 type_alias_statement, so the write never reaches the binder. It must preserve dev class-body lazy re-scope (GCLI-144/146) and must NOT create the F1 class-body edge (class C: type(x).m = helper(); from lib import helper -> dev refuses, and the re-dispatch created app.py:helper). The (a83)/(a84) fixtures and their observed-red control travel with it. (2) N8 from (a81) item 2: super() resolved by B static MRO only if every in-repo descendant orders the class after B identically, else receiver/needs-inference; a coarser any-multi-base test is allowed; removal-only; runtime-MRO modelling is NOT taken. Dev wrong edge measured 2026-11-27 at origin/dev 1ea3432: D(B, C) with B.m = super().m() gives A.m where a D instance reaches C.m. Expected files src/python/calls.ts and test/python-hops.test.ts. No DEC-182 path class, no dependency.

acceptanceCriteria.text: #4 re-dispatches type(x).m and type(self).m as attribute writes without creating the F1 class-body edge and without changing dev class-body lazy re-scope (GCLI-144/146), with the (a83)/(a84) fixtures and an observed-red control

N8 resolves super() by the static MRO only when every in-repo descendant orders the class after B identically, else receiver/needs-inference, with both base orders and a diamond fixture, and a mutant per path observed red

Removal-only holds: the flag-extended subset check over the five pins, every fixture and the corpus shows no created and no flag-changed in-repo edge, group count stated with a floor equal to the exact count, an observed-red control and every removed edge named in the PR
No DEC-182 path class is touched and no dependency is added

implementationNotes: Scope addition from the leader relay of DEC-303 (a82) item 2: the (a82) non-enumerable alias blind spot rides this task as MEASURE-FIRST, not a build. Quote: an alias whose binding cannot be enumerated is named in the PR body as a blind spot and goes into GCLI-156 measurement; it is not built here. Measure occurrence on the five pins with a positive control (read-only, as (a81) item 3); build only if the measurement shows a reachable wrong edge and it fits two rounds, otherwise name it in the PR body as a documented blind spot.

WATCH ITEMS from #248 round 1 (N-f and the dev-equal holes N-a/N-b/N-c), to scope BEFORE building; not part of the #4/N8 build. N-f: the cls.__class__.m over-refusal (test/python-hops.test.ts, the test at ~:3083) was accepted by (a84) and was labelled "fix in GCLI-156"; it was neither fixed there nor carried, so it lands here. N-a: a write recorded on a MIXIN is invisible to the #6 guard (class C(B, Mix) where Mix writes self.m); a fix would walk each descendant own MRO as the class-attribute paths do. N-b: a class-body binding on a descendant (class C(B): m = 2) is neither a recorded write nor a def, so the guard does not see it. N-c: c = C(); c.m = 2 goes to addLocalAttrWrite, not classAttrWrites, so the guard does not see it. All three are dev-equal holes, not this PR; measure first if any is taken.

ROUND-2 NON-BLOCKING CARRIES from opum-ai/glyph-cli#248 (recorded after it landed at dev 4b29ee7; not pushed to #248). (a) Pin the N-d reason labels: the two N-d fixtures assert bins only, exactly as the kit compares bins and not reasons; add the unresolvedReceiverReasons assertion (needs-inference:1 on the written side, empty on the twin) the way the N1 fixture does. (b) The #6 comment at calls.ts says resolveModuleChain stays live "inside the wrapped read", but its call runs after the wrap returns, so the sentence is wording-only; correct it when the file is next touched. (c) N-e, round 1 lettering, unfixtured removal-only over-refusal: B().m(), x = B(); x.m(), B.m(o), h = B.m; h(), and f = B(); f() (__call__) never see a descendant instance and fall back to a name bin. List as a watch item; scope before building, do not add to the #4/N8 build silently.

MEASURE-FIRST (a82 non-enumerable alias blind spot, per DEC-303 (a82) item 2 and (a88)). Method: a disposable copy of this tree with a counter at exactly the path aliasWriteTargets names the blind spot (enumerableBindings === null), run over the five pins at the proof-kit SHAs. RESULT: 483 files, exactly ONE lookup reaches it — rich/tests/test_repr.py:55, `__rich_repr__.angular = True`, a FUNCTION-attribute write inside a DECORATED class body (undecorated class bodies do not reach this path at all). No non-enumerable ALIAS write exists on the pins. CONTROLS: the same instrument fires on a decorated class holding `def f` plus `f.angular = True`, and fires on nothing for the enumerable alias `K = C; K.m = 1`. DECISION: no reachable wrong edge (no reader resolves a call through that function attribute) and it does not fit two rounds with #4/N8, so it is documented as a blind spot in the PR body and NOT built.

BUILD on branch fix/GCLI-164-type-redispatch-and-super-mro, cut from dev 815a23f. (1) #4: the type_alias_statement case detects the misparsed assignment (an attribute on the left), records it as a write with describeCallee typeArg, keeps dev climbed-name rebound binding marked typeAliasMisparse (reads see it, the write classification ignores it through receiverOfIgnoringMisparse), and then falls through to the SHARED alias tail so the value keeps the lazy class-body scope (GCLI-144/146). Unshadowed `type` required. (2) N8: methodLookup on the fromSuper path refuses when any in-repo descendant orders a different tail after the receiver (superOrderDiffers), fail-closed on an uncomputable descendant MRO; D(C, B) keeps its edge because its tail matches, the diamond D(B, C) refuses. FIXTURES: #4 written/twin, nested-def control, shadowed type, F1 import-later and def-later (measured dev-equal on dev 58255fc, on 98e09e7 and on this head — the reported F1 helper edge did not reproduce on any of the three), local x control; N8 diamond B,C / C,B / linear / none / two-arg. RED BEFORE on dev: self.m() resolves where the type(self).m fixture refuses; the diamond gives A.m where the build refuses; two-arg gives A.m where the build refuses.

MUTANTS, each observed red with its predicted subset: M24 superOrderDiffers call off -> N8 diamond and two-arg (2); M25 over-coarse any-descendant -> D(C,B) and the linear twin (2); M26 the #4 write recording off -> item-2 #4, type(self) refusal and the subclass case (3); M28 the unshadowed-type guard off -> the shadowed-type fixture (1); M29 the misparse-binding filter off -> type(self) refusal and item-2 #4 (2). M27 (skip the shared lazy reparent for the misparse) changes nothing observed: the F1 shapes measure dev-equal on dev 58255fc, on 98e09e7 and on this head, so it is a dev-equal fixture, not a red-before, and is labelled so.

PROOF: subset155.ts extended with 12 GCLI-164 fixtures (122 total, was 110); 1521 groups at floor 1521 (5 pins + 1394 corpus + 122 fixtures). dev 17560 edges, head 17552. 0 created, 0 flag-changed. 8 removed edges, every one a fixture: B1 and the four GCLI-156 #6 refusals (from the prior PR, still in the kit), GCLI-164 #4 type(self) written app.py:7:9->app.py:C.m, and N8 diamond B,C plus two-arg app.py:6:16->app.py:A.m. 10 bin changes: those 8 plus N-d dict and N-d opaque. Pins unmoved (flask 1366, httpx 2791, jinja 2833, rich 7410, tqdm 981). Controls: --control FAILs on 2 injected created edges; --floor-control FAILs at 1521 < 1e6; compare_notes OK on all 1521 groups and --control detects an injected note. Kit subset155.ts sha256 and head calls.ts sha256 recorded in the PR body.
finalSummary:
Landed on branch fix/GCLI-164-type-redispatch-and-super-mro, cut from dev 815a23f. Scope: #4 (DEC-303 (a84) item 1), (a81) item 2 N8, and the (a82) non-enumerable alias blind spot as measure-first. #4: the type_alias_statement case detects the attribute-on-the-left misparse, records a class-level write on the receiver class (describeCallee typeArg plus receiverOfIgnoringMisparse), keeps dev climbed-name rebound binding marked typeAliasMisparse so reads stay dev-equal, falls through to the shared alias tail so the value keeps GCLI-144/146 lazy class-body scope, and keeps the unshadowed-type guard. Red before on dev: type(self).m resolves C.m where this head refuses, and a subclass flips to refused through the ancestor guard; nested-def, local x, shadowed type all stay dev-equal. F1 was MEASURED, not forced: the reported helper edge did not reproduce on dev 58255fc, on 98e09e7 (the removed re-dispatch) or on this head; the fixture pins the measured dev-equal answer and is labelled so. N8: superOrderDiffers refuses when any in-repo descendant orders a different tail after the receiver, fail-closed on an uncomputable descendant MRO; the diamond D(B, C) and the two-argument form refuse on dev A.m, while D(C, B), linear, no-descendant and unrelated twins still resolve. a82: instrumented the exact blind-spot path over the five pins — 483 files, ONE site (rich/tests/test_repr.py:55, a function-attribute write in a decorated class body), no non-enumerable alias, positive and negative controls both fire; no reachable wrong edge, documented in the PR and not built. Mutants M24/M25/M26/M28/M29 each observed red on its predicted subset. Proof: 1521 groups at floor 1521, 0 created, 0 flag-changed, 8 removed edges (each a named fixture) and 10 bin changes, pins unmoved, both controls and the notes comparator firing; bun run check exits 0 with 1376 tests. No DEC-182 path class, no dependency.

ROUND 1 on #250 found that this record closed with its own carries open (B2). The carries and watch items — N-f the cls.__class__.m over-refusal, N-a the mixin write, N-b the descendant class-body binding, N-c the local receiver write, N-e the removal-only over-refusals, and the nested-def blind spot — are re-carried to GCLI-151 and the test comment at ~:3089 points there. The N-d reason labels are pinned in the fixture (needs-inference:1 written, none in the twin) and the resolveModuleChain wording is corrected in calls.ts.

ROUND-1 FIX: the class-level branch now requires the misparse mark, so setattr(type(self), "m", v), del type(self).m, type(self).m += v and type(cls).m stay dev-equal and are fixtured (M30 reddens them). (a83) item 2 now constructs after the write, N8 pins a neighbour super().n() and D().m() with reason labels, superOrderDiffers fails closed when a descendant MRO cannot name the receiver (measured: no pin edge moves), and the proof is re-run at 1526 groups (127 fixtures) with 0 created, 0 flag-changed, 10 removed fixture edges, pins unmoved and all controls firing. bun run check exits 0 with 1378 tests.
